Baltimore investigators handed over their files on Freddie Gray's death to prosecutors Thursday, but the public should not expect immediate charges or answers. The process is largely procedural, and officials have emphasized that the investigation must remain full and complete before any charges are filed. Mayor Stephanie Rawlings-Blake reiterated that releasing information hastily could jeopardize the probe, stating it "cannot be the end" since there have been no charges or trials yet.

Robert Downey Jr. abruptly ended an interview with British journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy after the reporter asked about the actor's past addiction and jail time. Downey grew visibly agitated and condescending before standing up and walking out, declaring "bye!" after being asked if he was "free from all of that." The incident sparked debate online about the boundaries of celebrity interviews and a journalist's right to ask probing questions.

German police thwarted a terrorist plot by a radicalized Turkish couple who planned to bomb a major bicycle race near Frankfurt on May Day. Authorities recovered bomb-making materials, including a pipe bomb and hydrogen peroxide, and suspect the pair had ties to radical Islamist circles. The couple was arrested in Oberursel, and police believe the attack was intended to cause mass casualties along the race route.

Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe will address a joint session of Congress on Wednesday, marking the first time a Japanese leader has done so. The visit is significant as it coincides with efforts to advance the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade agreement, which aims to expand U.S. influence in Asia. However, the trip faces political hurdles, as Congress must first reauthorize "trade promotion authority" to finalize the deal, a measure that has divided lawmakers despite bipartisan support for free trade.

When Gabriel Salvador, a waiter and actor, mentioned to CBS CEO Les Moonves that his son trained under Manny Pacquiao's trainer, Freddie Roach, he sparked a connection that helped facilitate the long-awaited Floyd Mayweather vs. Manny Pacquiao fight. Salvador's efforts in introducing the two sides eventually led to him being invited to sit ringside for the historic May 2 pay-per-view event. While Pacquiao's team downplayed his contribution, Salvador views the experience as his reward, emphasizing that he simply wanted to help make the fight happen.

Kim Bok-dong, an 89-year-old former "comfort woman," is fighting to share her harrowing experiences of sexual slavery at the hands of the Japanese army before she passes away. Despite her frail health and failing eyesight, she remains determined to set the record straight about the past, insisting that an apology is long overdue. She continues to speak out through the Korean Council for the Women Drafted for Military Sexual Slavery by Japan, seeking justice for the systemic abuse she and other women endured.

A devastating earthquake in Nepal has killed over 4,600 people and injured more than 9,000, with eight million affected and one million children in urgent need of aid. The disaster was compounded by a landslide in Langtang National Park that left up to 200 people missing. Relief efforts are ongoing but hampered by logistical challenges and severe weather, as survivors face the additional trauma of aftershocks and heavy rain.

A joint Indian Air Force and Nepalese army relief mission delivered critical supplies and evacuated injured survivors to Kathmandu following the devastating 7.8-magnitude earthquake. Local officials report the situation in Melamchi is "dire," with thousands displaced and lacking adequate food and medical care. The operation highlights the urgent need for more aid as many injured residents remain stranded in local clinics waiting for evacuation.

Judge Jerry Baxter reduced the prison sentences of three Atlanta educators convicted in the cheating scandal from seven years to three years, citing personal discomfort with the severity of the original terms. The three defendants—Tamara Cotman, Sharon Davis-Williams, and Michael Pitts—were also ordered to serve seven years of probation, pay $10,000 fines, and complete 2,000 hours of community service.

A dozen Native American actors walked off the set of Adam Sandler's "The Ridiculous Six" on Wednesday, citing offensive and stereotypical portrayals of Native women and culture. The actors, including Navajo performer Allison Young, protested script elements like demeaning names and degrading scenes, feeling their dignity was disrespected despite Netflix's defense of the film as satire. The walkout highlights ongoing tensions over representation, with the actors asserting they were told to leave if they were "sensitive" about the content.

A wave of anti-immigrant violence in South Africa has left several dead and forced thousands, including Congolese immigrant Tarsis Mboma Thale, to seek refuge at police stations and shelters. The unrest, fueled by high unemployment and alleged inflammatory rhetoric, has prompted President Jacob Zuma to deploy troops and sparked fears among foreign nationals that they are being targeted simply for living and working in the country. While some blame the Zulu king's comments or past labor disputes, many, like Eric Kalonji, argue the violence stems from the government's failure to provide jobs and education

Indianapolis police command staff will begin wearing white uniforms starting Friday to enhance transparency and accountability. The change aims to make senior leaders more identifiable to the public, serving as a "final point of contact" during a time of increased scrutiny. While not a total department overhaul, the shift is intended to project professionalism and accessibility amid nationwide protests over police tactics.

Bryan Singer announced via Instagram that Olivia Munn will play the telepathic Psylocke in "X-Men: Apocalypse," joining a cast that includes James McAvoy and Jennifer Lawrence. The film, set for a summer 2016 release, will see Munn portray Betsy Braddock, the British mutant who has been a mainstay in X-Men comics since 1987.

Photographer Laurence Rasti documented the lives of Iranian LGBT refugees in Denizli, Turkey, capturing their struggle with identity and limbo after fleeing persecution. Despite the constant threat of execution and social stigma, the refugees maintain hope while waiting years for resettlement in a third country. Rasti's project aims to restore their stolen identities through anonymous portraits, highlighting their resilience despite being forced to lie to their families about their reasons for leaving.

Hawkeye, the Marvel superhero played by Jeremy Renner, surprised audiences on "The Tonight Show" by showcasing his singing talents with a parody of Ed Sheeran's "Thinking Out Loud." Beyond his archery skills, Renner revealed he can play the trombone, open pickle jars, and sport an impressive collection of scarves and berets. The appearance highlighted the actor's versatility, proving he is "more than a one-hit wonder" with a diverse career spanning blockbuster franchises and Oscar-winning films.

A group of fighters in Afghanistan were filmed by CNN pledging allegiance to ISIS, marking the first such imagery captured by Western media inside the country. The rise of the group is fueled by disillusioned Taliban fighters and young men seeking an alternative, despite the Afghan government previously downplaying the threat. U.S. officials express concern over the potential for an ISIS presence, noting the group has limited capability but is actively trying to recruit from the ranks of the Taliban.

Baltimore City State's Attorney Marilyn Mosby, a former insurance lawyer and the first African-American to hold the position, now faces the difficult decision of whether to file criminal charges against six police officers involved in the death of Freddie Gray. Mosby, who took office in January, has pledged to conduct an independent investigation rather than rely solely on the police's findings, asking the public to remain peaceful while the justice process unfolds. The case has drawn national attention to police-community relations, especially after Gray's death sparked protests and riots in the majority-black city.

Jared Leto's new portrayal of the Joker in "Suicide Squad" has become an internet sensation, sparking a wave of memes and comparisons shortly after the character's reveal. Set for an August 5, 2016 release, the film also stars Will Smith and Margot Robbie, with social media users quickly putting their Photoshopping skills to work on the new look.

Jay Z took to Twitter to defend his new music streaming service, Tidal, against criticism that it is underperforming compared to competitors like Spotify. The rapper used the hashtag #TidalFacts to refute negative talk, though his efforts were met with some derision and a parody account was quickly created. The service, launched with much fanfare by artists including Beyoncé and Kanye West, aims to be the first artist-owned global music platform.

Thousands remain missing in Nepal following a devastating earthquake, including tourists and locals, as families scramble to locate loved ones using social media and technology. While the death toll has surpassed 5,000, stories of survival persist, such as a woman who trekked for six hours through dangerous terrain to reach safety and reunite with her family.

Former rap mogul Marion "Suge" Knight pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges related to a fatal hit-and-run in Compton. The judge denied his attorney's request to reduce his $10 million bail, citing the severity of the charges. Knight faces up to life in prison if convicted for running over two men during an argument at a burger stand.

Stephen Hawking has teamed up with Monty Python to recreate the "Galaxy Song" for Record Store Day, featuring a humorous showdown with scientist Brian Cox. The collaboration highlights Hawking's signature wit, blending his computerized voice with a lesson on the cosmos while poking fun at the song's scientific inaccuracies.

Iran's Basij militia and Revolutionary Guard are actively involved in the fight against ISIS, training and supporting Iraqi Shia militias, though they remain wary of U.S. intentions. While Iranian officials believe their strategy is effective and call for better cooperation, the U.S. denies direct coordination, viewing Iran's involvement with suspicion despite shared goals against the group.

Universal announced that "Fifty Shades Darker" will release on February 10, 2017, with the third film following on February 9, 2018. The news comes after Niall Leonard, the husband of author E.L. James, was tapped to write the sequel's script, and stars Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are reportedly negotiating for higher pay following the first film's massive $568.8 million global success.

As the "Great Kate Wait" continues, betting heavily favors the arrival of a baby girl, who would be significant not only for the economic boost to the British High Street but also for providing a much-needed female presence in a monarchy currently dominated by men. While the child is unlikely to rule, her arrival would offer a powerful symbolic counterpoint to a history of kings, potentially mirroring the progressive legacies of past Queen Elizabeths and reinforcing the importance of female leadership within the institution.

People magazine named Sandra Bullock the "World's Most Beautiful Woman" for 2015, celebrating her as the oldest recipient in the list's history. The cover story highlights her focus on inner beauty, family life with her son, and maintaining health and confidence past 40. Bullock, who called the honor "ridiculous," emphasized that true beauty comes from being a good person and staying happy rather than focusing on appearance.

As the world anticipates the birth of William and Kate's second child, speculation is rife over potential names, with Diana emerging as a sentimental favorite despite her polarizing legacy. While some view naming the baby after Princess Diana as a heartfelt tribute, others see it as a potential slight to the monarchy, given the late princess's divisive reputation. Ultimately, the couple is unlikely to choose the name out of respect for the Queen and the complex emotions Diana's name still evokes.

Linda Thompson, Bruce Jenner's second wife, expressed relief that he has publicly come out as transgender, stating he can now "realize his need to be who he authentically is." She revealed that Jenner had identified as a woman since 1985 but had kept it secret, and she credits his courage for allowing him to live authentically. Thompson also reflected that she would not have married him had she known earlier, but is grateful she didn't, as it allowed her to share a life with him and their two sons.

Bernie Sanders has officially launched his presidential campaign, positioning himself as an authentic, fearless voice who has long understood the concerns of ordinary Americans. While he remains a long shot to win the nomination, his run represents a significant challenge to the political establishment, driven by his passionate advocacy for progressive policies and his deep connection to the working class.

With Washington gridlocked, liberal Democrats are increasingly turning to state and local governments to advance their agenda. While federal progress has stalled, cities and states are pioneering initiatives in pre-K education, housing, and minimum wage increases. This shift allows for "functionality of politics" where local action can solve problems despite national partisan gridlock.

Rescuers in Nepal pulled a 15-year-old boy from the rubble after he had been buried for five days, celebrating his survival as a "miracle." A U.S. special operations team also evacuated 30 people, including three Americans, by helicopter from a remote village where they were trapped.

Here is the information for the Aston Villa versus Queens Park Rangers game:

**Team News**
*   **Aston Villa:** The manager, Tim Sherwood, will be without three important players. Alan Hutton, Scott Sinclair, and Ashley Westwood are all unavailable for the match.

**Match Details**
*   **Location:** The game is at Aston Villa's home ground, Villa Park.
*   **Opponent:** Queens Park Rangers.

Kim Sei-young is leading the ANA Inspiration tournament. On Saturday in California, she shot a 69, which was three under par. This gave her a three-shot lead going into the final round. She started well by birdieing the first hole, but then made a bogey at the fifth hole. She recovered by birdieing the ninth hole. Birdies on the 16th and 17th holes finished her round at three under par for the day, putting her 10 under par overall.

Tiger Woods wants to win, but it would be a disaster if he plays at the Masters while injured. This is the opinion of Colin Montgomerie. Woods confirmed he is returning to competitive golf for the first time since February, when he withdrew from a tournament with a back injury. He has fallen to 104th in the world rankings and has not played a real match since then. Besides some practice in Florida and at Augusta, he has no competitive experience. Even so, Woods said earlier this week that he will play at the Masters.

Last year, Liverpool had a strong attack. Luis Suarez and Daniel Sturridge scored a lot of goals together—52 in total. This year, the goals have stopped. It was always hard to replace Suarez, but fans hoped the team could make up for his absence. Unfortunately, the team has not been scoring as well as they did last year.

The Miami Open is celebrating a lot like it is "Cake Week." This happened after Serena Williams won her 700th career match. The day after Andy Murray won his 500th match, a giant cake was brought out to celebrate Williams reaching the semi-finals. She won her match against Sabine Lisicki with a score of 7-6, 1-6, 6-3. Even though her sister Venus lost and ended Serena's chance to play her, Serena kept playing because this tournament is like a hometown event for her. After winning her 700th match, Serena Williams posed next to her cake.

Andy Murray has a simple message for British tennis players who are upset about Aljaz Bedene joining them: don't complain. Murray thinks his colleagues should use Bedene's arrival as motivation to improve their own game. Right now, any complaints are happening quietly. This is because Bedene is currently not allowed to play for the Davis Cup team, but this could change if the International Tennis Federation approves his request to play. Aljaz Bedene was photographed at his British citizenship ceremony in Hatfield on Tuesday morning.

South Korea's Kim Sei-young made a spectacular eagle on the 18th hole in the second round of the ANA Inspiration on Friday. This put her two shots ahead. The 22-year-old player, who won her first LPGA Tour title in February, hit a great second shot that landed six feet from the hole. She then made the putt to score a seven-under-par 65. This gave her a total of seven-under 137, which was two shots better than overnight leader Morgan Pressel. Lydia Ko's chance at a record-equaling run ended when her ball landed in the water on the 18th hole.

Nick Scholfield is scheduled to ride the horse Spring Heeled in the Grand National at Aintree on April 11. He was originally supposed to ride the horse for Jim Culloty in the Crabbie’s Grand National on Saturday.

Scholfield was previously expected to ride Sam Winner, a horse trained by Paul Nicholls, in a one million pound race. However, Sam Winner was pulled up during the Cheltenham Gold Cup. On Wednesday, the champion trainer Paul Nicholls said it was unfair to assign Scholfield to Spring Heeled, a gelding that might not run, when another leading horse was available to ride.

Novak Djokovic, the defending champion, won a tough match against Alexandr Dolgopolov to reach the quarter-finals of the Miami Open.

Dolgopolov, who is ranked 65th in the world, took the first set in a tie-break and led 4-2 in the second set. However, Djokovic fought back to win the next two sets and the match.

Djokovic will now play in the quarter-finals.

Newport Gwent Dragons beat Cardiff Blues 25-21 to reach the European Challenge Cup semi-finals. 

Tries were scored by Hallam Amos, Nic Cudd, and a penalty try. Tom Prydie and Dorian Jones kicked penalties, and Prydie also scored two conversions. For Cardiff, Lloyd Williams, Gareth Anscombe, and Josh Navidi scored tries, with Anscombe kicking three conversions.

An Australian kangaroo escaped and hopped away in West Germany. Police in Rhein Erft got a strange call about a kangaroo hopping in a field. At first, they thought it was an April Fools joke. However, they later found the kangaroo in Bruhl.

Social media is talking about a mistake on Channel 7 during a big Australian charity show. TV hosts were not aware that a man named Hugh G. Rection donated $32.38. His name appeared on screen, and Twitter users quickly noticed. The Royal Children’s Hospital’s Good Friday Appeal raised over $17.1 million for research and facilities. This is a record amount, which is more than the $16.8 million donated last year.

Carla Suarez Navarro from Spain came back to defeat Venus Williams 0-6, 6-1, 7-5 at the Miami Open on Tuesday. This victory sent her into the semi-finals, where she will face Germany's Andrea Petkovic.

Petkovic reached the semi-finals by beating Karolina Pliskova 6-4, 6-2. Williams completely dominated the first set, winning it 6-0 in under thirty minutes. However, Suarez Navarro regrouped and played impressively to win the next two sets and the match.

Somerset's new limited-overs captain, Alfonso Thomas, has agreed to coach the Delhi Daredevils in the Indian Premier League this month. Thomas is still recovering from a broken ankle, so he is not fit to play for Somerset in their first County Championship match at home to Durham. However, his club has agreed to let him take the short-term coaching job with Delhi until April 16.

Bath will use their English players to try to beat Leinster in Dublin. They want to make up for their Six Nations loss to Ireland at the Aviva Stadium last month. Players like George Ford, Dave Attwood, Jonathan Joseph, and Anthony Watson were in that 19-9 defeat. Their coach thinks that loss might help them in the Champions Cup quarter-final. Jonathan Joseph will play for Bath in Dublin, and he wants to prove himself after England's defeat.

Andy Murray is playing in the semi-finals of the Miami Open. He had to play an Austrian player named Dominic Thiem, who is 21 years old. Thiem pushed Murray very close, making the score 4-4 in the second set, but Murray eventually won the match 3-6, 6-4, 6-1. Before this tournament, Thiem had lost a match to a British player named Aljaz Bedene. Murray is still in the tournament because he wants to finish his tennis business before his wedding next week. He is currently ranked world number four. He is waiting to find out who he will play in the semi-finals, which will be either Tomas Berdych or Juan Monaco from Argentina.

The Sacramento Kings are signing Sim Bhullar to a 10-day contract. This will make him the first player of Indian descent to play in the NBA. The Kings plan to announce the deal on Thursday, when another player's contract expires. Bhullar, who is 7-foot-5 and weighs 360 pounds, is joining the team from their development league affiliate in Reno.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall says the club's removal from the London Stock Exchange will not stop the team from chasing promotion. The club was taken off the AIM market on Thursday after new chairman-in-waiting Dave King could not find a replacement advisor. Interim chairman Paul Murray said the previous board was to blame, but he revealed the new owners are looking at moving to a different market called ISDX. McCall was at a training session on Good Friday.

Moeen Ali is planning to join the England team later in their Test tour of the West Indies. His side injury is getting better. He hurt himself during England's World Cup campaign and was not picked for the Caribbean squad because of it. Moeen was dismissed during a World Cup match against New Zealand. Last summer, he had a successful start to Test cricket, taking 22 wickets in seven matches.

Manager Arsene Wenger believes something special is finally happening at Arsenal. After a 4-1 win over Liverpool at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, the team has won seven games in a row. This victory moved them up to second place in the league. While Manchester City could take second place by beating Crystal Palace on Monday, and Chelsea still leads the team by seven points, Wenger is confident that with all his players available, Arsenal can beat anyone.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino believes goalkeeper Michel Vorm has the strength to recover from his Capital One Cup final disappointment. He will play for Burnley on Sunday because first-choice goalkeeper Hugo Lloris is injured. Vorm, 31, joined Tottenham from Swansea in the summer. He was on the bench at the League Cup final in London last month, despite playing in earlier rounds. Now he is ready to replace Lloris in goal.

Celtic striker Leigh Griffiths ate a Tunnock's Tea Cake before his team's game against St Mirren on Good Friday. He ate the biscuit on the bench during the first ten minutes of the match. His manager, Ronnie Deila, encourages players to follow a strict diet. Griffiths was seen looking around the dug-out before eating the snack.

Porto has sold players for a total of £440 million over the last 11 years. Since winning the Champions League in 2004, the club has made a habit of selling players for large profits. This is largely because of lenient work permit laws in Portugal, which allow many South American players to play there. The most recent sale was right back Danilo, who joined Real Madrid in the summer for £23 million. Jose Mourinho was the coach when Porto won the 2004 Champions League.

Lionel Messi's foot is still swollen, which is worrying Barcelona. He missed two games for Argentina during the break. Now, he must take tests to see if he can play against Celta Vigo on Sunday.

Spanish newspaper SPORT put this story on their front cover. They say Messi wants to play because Barcelona is chasing the La Liga title. However, he is not certain to play. Tests on Thursday will decide his fate. His teammate Gerard Pique thinks he might play, but another newspaper, AS, says he is a "doubt."

River Plate wants to sign Radamel Falcao from Manchester United. The Colombian striker played for River Plate for eight years before moving to Porto in 2009. River Plate's vice president, Matias Patanian, said they "dream" of having Falcao back. However, a deal is complicated because Falcao has had a hard time performing while on loan at Manchester United.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers says he gives young players like Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe a chance because he knows what it is like to be rejected.

Rodgers left Northern Ireland for England at 16 to train with Reading's youth team. He did not become a professional player, even though he was promised a first-team spot. He believes this experience helps him understand and support Liverpool's young talent.

Stephen Curry scored 27 points and Klay Thompson had 25 as the Golden State Warriors won 110-106 against the Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday. This was the Warriors' 10th straight win. David Lee added 17 points for Golden State.

The Clippers lost despite blowing a 17-point lead. Their seven-game winning streak ended. Blake Griffin scored 40 points and got 12 rebounds. Chris Paul had 27 points and nine assists. J.J. Redick scored 14.

The Warriors had lost four games in a row at Staples Center before this win. Drake was courtside at the game.

Former Liverpool player Jamie Carragher went to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play in a youth tournament. He traveled to Girona in northern Spain to watch the Under 12s Mediterranean International Cup, which has teams from 36 countries. While there, Carragher spoke to local TV and posted a photo from the opening ceremony on Instagram.

Finally, some good news for Sunderland and Newcastle United. It turns out that form goes out the window when these two teams play each other. Isn't that a relief?

On Sunday, the fans will get to forget about their team's bad run of form. Over their last six matches (12 games total), the teams have only managed to score six points. During that same time—18 hours of football—they have scored four goals but conceded 22. It is no wonder they have called this match "The Desperation Derby." Perhaps "The Donkey Derby" would be a better name.

Real Madrid star James Rodriguez is back and will play against Granada on Sunday. He missed two months because of a broken right foot, but he is now fit. Manager Carlo Ancelotti said James looks good in training and will start the game. He will play in the attack alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale.

Bayern Munich player Thiago came back to play for the first time in a year during a game against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday. The midfielder had not played since March 2014, when he hurt his knee. He came into the game for Philipp Lahm, and Bayern won 1-0. Thiago said the fans' reaction reminded him how much he loves football. He stated, "Football is my life."

St Etienne wants to buy Cardiff full-back Kevin Theophile-Catherine permanently. The 25-year-old joined Cardiff from Stade Rennais for £2.1 million and has been on loan at St Etienne this season. St Etienne can make the deal permanent for £1.5 million, but Theophile-Catherine wants to wait and see if other clubs want him before signing. He has two years left on his contract at Cardiff.

Separately, St Etienne will not make Ricky Van Wolfswinkel's move from Norwich permanent. The Dutch striker scored only one goal after joining on loan for £8.

Former Huddersfield centre Josh Griffin scored a try and kicked three goals. Salford secured back-to-back Super League wins with an 18-12 victory at the John Smith's Stadium.

Griffin and Ben Jones-Bishop scored tries in the first half. Jack Hughes gave the Giants hope, but Carl Forster's try and Griffin's penalty made the game safe. Despite Aaron Murphy's try, Salford Red Devils won 18-12.

Salford made a fast start, but Cory Paterson had a try ruled out on 18 minutes.

Rangi Chase, a player for Salford, might be banned for four to eight matches after he was charged with a dangerous throw during a game on Good Friday. Salford won the game 18-12 against Huddersfield, but they may lose Chase for a long time. The Rugby Football League reviewed the tackle and wants Chase to appear before a tribunal on Wednesday.

Andros Townsend is a player who changes between being excellent and not trying hard very often. He is doing well now after scoring a great goal for England against Italy on Tuesday. The 23-year-old winger for Tottenham has had many more highs and lows than most players. On a good day, he is as good as the best players. He scares defenders with his speed. He also showed this off the pitch with a 'told you so' tweet to Paul Merson this week. People first noticed his talent two years ago when he tried to save QPR from going down with great plays.

Warrington lost their third game in a row in the Super League. During the Cheshire derby against Widnes, a flare was thrown from the stands, stopping the game for eight minutes. Despite the delay, Widnes won 30-10 and kept their strong home form. Warrington's Matty Russell got injured, and the team is now on their worst losing streak since 2009. The Rugby Football League is also investigating the crowd trouble.

England have finally arrived home from Turin after a delayed flight landed at Manchester Airport on Tuesday night. The team had originally planned to leave northern Italy immediately after their 1-1 draw with Italy, but a technical problem with their plane forced them to stay one extra night.

The squad stopped in Manchester to let northern-based players and staff off before heading to London. Players from Manchester United, Manchester City, Everton, Liverpool, Aston Villa, and Stoke City all left to rejoin their clubs ahead of the Barclays Premier League matches this weekend.

Wigan moved up to third place in the Super League by beating their rivals St Helens 12-4 at their home stadium. The match was a close and physical contest played on a wet pitch, with only three tries scored in front of 24,044 fans. Both teams played hard, and the players were very tired by the end of the game. Dom Manfredi scored Wigan's first try.

Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport criticized Theo Walcott's performance against Italy. They gave him a score of five out of ten, the lowest of the English players. England captain Wayne Rooney, goalscorer Andros Townsend, and substitute Ross Barkley all received a seven out of ten. Italy's boss Antonio Conte was praised for his team's 1-1 draw.

Daryl Clark, the current captain of Warrington, will play against his old team, Castleford, on Easter Monday. Clark grew up playing for Castleford but left at the end of last season. He is eager to face his former club but will be watching closely to see how they are doing. He previously broke his nose in a game against Widnes, but he is expected to be fit for the match.

Brendan Rodgers says Raheem Sterling will not leave Liverpool this summer. He is relaxed about the player's contract situation. Sterling recently gave a TV interview where he said he is not ready to sign a new £100,000-a-week deal, which caused transfer rumors. Although Rodgers said the interview surprised him because it was done without the club's permission, he believes Sterling is still young and sometimes makes mistakes.

England's Joe Hart called Italy's Gianluigi Buffon a "legend of the game" after Buffon played his 147th match for his country. Hart, who reached his 50th appearance for England on Tuesday, said Buffon was an inspiration. Hart told FA TV that he still learns from watching Buffon, who is 37 years old.

Graziano Pelle joined Southampton from Feyenoord for about £9 million. He started playing well, scoring nine goals in his first 12 games. However, he has not scored in the Premier League since December 20.

On Tuesday, Pelle played for Italy against England. He scored the first goal by heading Giorgio Chiellini's cross into Joe Hart's far corner. This gave Italy a 1-0 lead.

Five staff members were seriously injured at the Sydney Royal Easter Show on Saturday night after riding the Super Slide. The slide was closed because of heavy rain, but a group of eight workers broke in and went down the 52-metre slide anyway. The workers were supposed to be keeping the slide closed due to the dangerous conditions.

Saints lost badly to Clermont at Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday. This game showed how much richer French clubs are compared to English teams. It was a terrible result for Saints and for English rugby. Even though Saints are the best team in their own league, they were completely outplayed by Clermont at home. Clermont is almost impossible to beat at home, and Saints had no answer for them.

Zara Tindall, 33, is a professional horse rider. She tried wheelchair rugby, a sport nicknamed "murder ball," at last September's Invictus Games. Recently, she tried barrel-pulling during a charity event. She laughed while pretending to pull her husband, Mike, who is a 16-stone rugby player, for photos. The event marked the end of personal trainer Rob Edmond's marathon barrel-roll from Perthshire to Wiltshire. Zara put on Rob's barrel-pulling harness and pretended to pull the barrel while Mike posed on top of it.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini says the club must buy new young players because the Academy graduates are not yet ready for the first team. Liverpool star Raheem Sterling has been linked with a move to City because his contract at Anfield is stuck in a stalemate. Part of the pressure to sign fresh talent comes from FA chairman Greg Dyke, who wants to increase the number of homegrown players in Premier League squads to 12. Pellegrini does not think his current Academy players are good enough to play alongside stars like Yaya Toure. Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart made a save during training on Wednesday.

Teachers are planning to vote on whether to go on strike. The National Union of Teachers wants to protest about pay and school funding. If they vote for action, tens of thousands of teachers could walk out in the autumn. This might cause schools to close temporarily. A vote of all 300,000 members will happen after the election, and any strikes would likely start in September.

Borussia Dortmund's Nuri Sahin says Arsenal made a "great bid" to sign him, but he stayed in Germany because his family did not want to move to England. The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder, who is now back at Dortmund, was first linked with the club in 2005 when he played for the under-17s. He said Arsenal knew Dortmund would become a strong team again, and he is grateful they made the offer.

A 59-year-old man named Antonio Nuñez was charged with attacking his girlfriend with a pitchfork at their home in San Antonio, Texas, on Monday.

According to police, Nuñez and the woman were arguing when he allegedly stabbed her in the buttocks with the gardening tool. The woman managed to spray him in the eyes and ran to a neighbor's house to call 911. She is currently in the hospital recovering. Nuñez faces an aggravated assault charge.

Former Leeds and England coach Tony Smith says he was surprised when Kevin Sinfield decided to switch sports. However, Smith now thinks it is a great idea. Sinfield, 34, who is the best captain in Leeds' history, announced he will quit rugby league at the end of the season to join Yorkshire Carnegie. Carnegie is the sister club of the Rhinos. Sinfield is close to becoming the third highest scorer in rugby league history with 3,997 points. He told reporters he decided to leave because he did not want to play against the Rhinos, and he wants to help Carnegie return to the top league.

An unknown man stole a male peacock from a Texas neighborhood on Saturday. The man caught the bird on camera while it was showing off its feathers during a mating ritual. He grabbed the peacock by its claws and put him in a black SUV. The neighborhood of Beckley Club Estates in Dallas reported the theft.

These funny pictures show a tortoise trying to mate with a female. The male tortoise climbs onto the female's back. However, he loses his balance and falls over onto his back. He fails to mate with the female, and she leaves him behind.

A farmer caught a cute moment on video. A baby duck was grooming a lamb's wool coat. The video shows the sign of trust and friendship between the two animals. The lamb, named Winter, stood still with its head lowered. The duck walked around the front of the lamb and started pecking its head and neck. As the duckling got closer, the lamb kept its head lowered. The lamb clearly enjoyed the attention.

A Cold War bunker built to house civil servants during a nuclear attack has been turned into a luxury home worth £3.5 million. The property is in Chislehurst, a suburb in southeast London. It was built in 1951 for government officials. The site was chosen because it was a wooden area that provided secrecy, and the house has walls five feet thick.

Police are looking for three people who stole an ATM from a gas station in California last Friday. The theft happened at a Shell station on Ygnacio Valley Road in Walnut Creek. 

CCTV video shows one man distracting a cashier at the window. While he talks to the clerk, a second man runs a cable from the back of a white pickup truck to the ATM. Once the cable is attached, the truck speeds away and pulls the ATM off the wall. Sparks fly as the heavy machine is dragged across the pavement. The man talking to the clerk then runs to join the truck.

Tyler MacNiven won a million dollars on the TV show The Amazing Race. He and his fiancée, Kelly Hennigan, made a three-minute movie to tell people about their upcoming wedding. The video is like an action movie. In it, they wash up on a shore, fight "villains," and escape a big explosion. The video tells everyone that they should not make plans for September 26, 2015.

Veteran broadcaster Peter Alliss, 84, has caused controversy by saying that laws designed to stop golf clubs from discriminating against women have actually harmed the sport. He claims these rules have led to a drop in the number of women members. In the past, some clubs only allowed women to join if they played at specific times and paid a lower fee.

Winning the league championship used to make a manager safe in their job for a long time. However, this is no longer true. In fact, the last four managers to win the Premier League all lost their jobs the very next year—three were fired, and one retired. Based on recent events, it would not be a surprise if Manuel Pellegrini becomes the fifth manager to leave so soon. After Manchester City lost 2-1 to Crystal Palace, a sad-looking Pellegrini guided the team to their second Premier League title in three seasons back in May.

A journalist asked Arsene Wenger about a fake April Fools' Day story. MailOnline had reported that before the Arsenal vs. Liverpool game, the captains' pre-match talks would be streamed live. Although it was a joke, Wenger and the press were confused by the question at Thursday's conference.

Everton players Leighton Baines and Luke Garbutt visited Alder Hey Children's Hospital on Wednesday. They went there to make Easter better for sick children and their families. After training, the two gave out chocolate eggs and took pictures on the wards.

Baines said that giving out eggs might not seem very important compared to what the children are going through. However, he noted that the parents really appreciate the players just visiting and taking a break from the day.

Oscar is having a great time right now. The Chelsea forward won a Capital One Cup medal this season, and his team is leading the Premier League by six points. He also scored for Brazil in a 3-1 win over France. Before Chelsea played Stoke on Saturday, Oscar posted a funny picture on Instagram of him drinking from a bottle of sweets.

Carlisle United manager Keith Curle was very angry after his team lost 3-1 to Accrington Stanley. He criticized his players, saying some of them "don't deserve to be professionals." The team has now gone five games without a win and is only three points and two places above the danger zone in the league. Curle told the BBC that the team's "strength of character" in the changing room was very weak.

Yaya Toure was accused by Jamie Carragher of not moving out of the way of Jason Puncheon's free-kick, which stopped Manchester City from getting a point at Selhurst Park. Toure, who earns £200,000 a week, was in a five-man wall when Puncheon took the kick to make it 2-0. Sportsmail columnist Carragher said on Sky Sports that Toure should have tried to get hit by the ball. 'That is not acceptable when you go into a wall,' Carragher said. 'The other players are desperate to be hit in the face, but it was poor from Yaya Toure.'

A 20-year-old football fan has been banned for three years after running onto the pitch without a shirt and doing somersaults during his first game at the stadium. Charlie Sumner invaded the field at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup match last month. While his team was winning 3-0, Sumner did four front flips, landing on his back each time, before stewards tackled him.

Mesut Ozil returned to London after a break. He posted a photo of himself relaxing with his dog on Twitter. He wrote "Home Sweet Home" under the picture. On Sunday, Germany beat Georgia 2-0 in a World Cup qualifier. Ozil is now looking forward to the Premier League game against Liverpool this weekend.

Lionel Messi should be able to play for Barcelona against Celta Vigo on Sunday. This is good news because he is the top scorer in the league. He missed Argentina's friendly games because he hurt his foot in a match against Real Madrid last month. However, Barcelona defender Gerard Pique says Messi is okay and is optimistic he will play.

FIFA has announced that Football Association chairman Greg Dyke has returned a £16,000 watch he was given as a gift.

Dyke received the watch from the Brazilian FA during a FIFA Congress meeting in Sao Paulo while the World Cup was taking place. The Brazilian FA had given out 65 of these limited edition Parmigiani watches in goodie bags, and the total value of all the watches was more than £1 million.

When the watches were recalled, Dyke initially refused to give his back. He had promised to donate the watch to the FA's official charity partner, Breast Cancer Care, so it could be auctioned.

Tyler Walker, an 18-year-old striker, scored his first senior goal for Nottingham Forest during a game against Brentford on Monday. This goal tied him with his father, Des Walker, who scored once in 408 games for the club. Manager Dougie Freedman believes Tyler can be a key player for Forest for many years. While this was a cause for celebration, it is unlikely to match the overall scoring record of his father.

Veteran BBC commentator Peter Alliss has criticized the BBC for not trying harder to win the rights to show the Open Championship. He also said that recent laws giving women more rights in golf have "caused mayhem" and "b*****ed up the game for a lot of people." Recent legislation has indeed given women more rights at golf clubs, and both St Andrews and Royal St George's have voted to admit female members for the first time.

Amanda Beringer asked her brother Brad Fraser to make a toast at her wedding in Eagle Bay, south of Perth, because their father had passed away. Brad Fraser performed a funny song to welcome his new brother-in-law. In the song, he sang that once you get married, you are legally stuck and cannot turn back.

David Luiz might not play in Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League game against Barcelona because he hurt his hamstring on Sunday. The Brazilian defender left the field after 35 minutes during PSG's 3-2 win over Marseille. He injured his left leg while running away from an opponent. PSG was losing at the time, and David Luiz immediately told the bench he needed to come off.

A New Zealand man was surprised when his brother called him after being missing for ten years. John Daniel Tohill, 37, was last seen in 2005 when he left Nelson on Tasman Bay to travel north. On Tuesday, his brother Tobias received a call from John saying he would be visiting soon. This was the first time John had contacted his family since 2005. Over the years, his family had hired investigators and police, but because John was an adult and had disappeared on his own, there was little reason for police to ask the public for help.

A dad is teaching his four-month-old son, Noah, to "fly." Videos on YouTube show Noah balancing on his father's palm as he is lifted into the air. The baby keeps his body and legs straight while his arms stretch out. People watching laugh as they see the baby fly. Noah started doing this trick when he was only one month old.

A photographer named Lucy Garrod has explained how a contact lens almost left her blind in one eye. She developed a corneal ulcer, which is a sore on the clear surface of her eye, caused by a bacterial infection. Lucy had worn contacts since she was 15 without issues, but one day she woke up with an itchy and irritated right eye. The infection grew under her lens, causing the ulcer that damaged her vision.

A group of meerkats at the Indianapolis Zoo got ready for the NCAA championship game by trying out basketball. The zoo put a makeshift backboard and hoop in their pen. The meerkats stood on their back legs to look at the equipment, but they had to play on the hilly ground of their enclosure. People watching smiled at the animals. The zoo also had a basketball scavenger hunt for visitors over the weekend.

A baby girl watched a toy hen lay eggs in a YouTube video by Shkesi. The toy hen bounces up and down and pops out plastic eggs. When the first egg appeared, the baby cried with joy. When the third egg came, she shrieked and waved her arms. Before laying the eggs, the toy played a song that said, "I'm about to show you how it's done, laying eggs is so much fun."

A video shows a sudden snowstorm hitting a bridge and river in Russia. The storm happened in Krasnoyarsk, Siberia's third-largest city. A video maker filmed it from the riverbank. First, a large white cloud appeared. Then, the snow fell fast, covering the Kommunalnyi Bridge and the Yenisei River in seconds. The storm moved at 45 miles per hour. It grew quickly in size and covered the bridge instantly.

Dogs are usually good at playing fetch, especially when there is food involved. However, a Golden Retriever named Fritz from California seems to have bad hand-eye coordination. In a new video, Fritz wore bunny ears for Easter and tried to catch a hard-boiled egg in his mouth. He jumped up enthusiastically, but the egg missed his jaw, bounced off his chest, and landed on the grass instead. A defeated Fritz then hung his head low as his bunny ears fell to the ground.

A woman from Birmingham was stuck in Tenerife for two weeks after thieves stole her passport. She and her husband had gone to the island for a short break to celebrate her birthday and their anniversary. Even though they had flown there from East Midlands airport, Ryanair would not let her fly home because they thought she might be an illegal immigrant.

Christopher Dodd, 24, and Fay Purdham, 27, are getting married. They grew up playing football together as boys in Middlesbrough but lost touch as teenagers. Fay transitioned to become a woman at age 23. They recently reunited and are now a couple planning to marry.

Sir Nick Faldo is now certain that Rory McIlroy is lifting too many weights. This happened after McIlroy appeared to squeeze Faldo during a practice round at Augusta National. McIlroy is on the cover of Men's Health magazine and says he is "obsessed with the gym." Faldo, a three-time Masters champion, worries that too much weight training will hurt McIlroy's golf swing. Last week, Faldo told the Daily Telegraph that lifting heavy weights is not good for golf and that his heaviest lift was just his own body weight.

Three people survived a hot air balloon crash in Russia after it hit a transmission tower. Video shows the balloon catching the side of the tower, causing the basket with the instructor and two passengers to fall. They all went to the hospital with cuts and bruises, but doctors say they are stable. The crash happened in the Dmitrov district.

Graeme McDowell says he has sometimes needed to rest in a padded room because he struggled with the challenges at Augusta National. However, he is hopeful he can play better this week after recovering from an ankle injury. The injury forced him to withdraw from the Valero Texas Open last month. This was only the third time in his career he had to leave a tournament early, and he does not enjoy doing it. He admitted he was unsure how badly he was hurt and probably should have withdrawn from the pro-am on Wednesday.

Tiger Woods said he was ready to play in the Masters for a fifth time after practicing for 11 holes at Augusta National on Monday. Woods had only played in two events this year. In his first event, he shot an 82 and missed the cut. In his second event on February 5, he withdrew because of an injury after 11 holes. This break caused Woods to fall outside the world's top 100 golfers for the first time since 1996. His ranking continued to slide, dropping from 104th to 111st. He returned to action by warming up at Augusta National ahead of The Masters.

Notts County has appointed Ricardo Moniz as their new manager. Just a week ago, the club said he could not take the job because of family reasons. But on Tuesday, he signed a three-year contract. The 50-year-old Dutchman has six games to save the team from being relegated to League Two. Currently, the team is one point away from safety.

A mysterious Easter Bunny left a chocolate egg on the doorstep of every house in a village of 3,000 people. Residents in Alderholt, Dorset, woke up on Sunday to find the treats. Rob Wood, 67, said it was a lovely gesture. He explained that every house in the village received an egg. He added that it was the first time this had ever happened and that it must have taken a lot of effort to organize.

Ben Crenshaw will play in the Par 3 Contest at the Masters to honor Arnold Palmer. Palmer is resting at home because he hurt his shoulder. Even though he cannot play, the 85-year-old will still start the tournament on Thursday. Ben Crenshaw will join Jack Nicklaus and Gary Player in the event.

Dundee manager Paul Hartley is not worried about Dundee United's poor recent form before their Scottish Premiership derby on Wednesday. United have lost seven of their last nine matches, drawing the other two, and their last league win was on January 24 against Motherwell. Despite this, Hartley believes his team still has a good chance of winning, saying, "They've still got good players."

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood has promised to ignore his friend Chris Ramsey if he calls him before their important game on Tuesday. If Queens Park Rangers win at Villa Park, they will move above Villa and force them into the relegation zone. Ramsey used to work for Sherwood at Tottenham. This game is very important for both managers.

Tomas Berdych beat Juan Monaco 6-3, 6-4 in the Miami Open quarter-finals on Wednesday. This win set up a rematch with Andy Murray, who defeated Berdych in the Australian Open semi-final last year. Monaco played well, but Berdych took control of the second set to win comfortably.

World No. 2 Roger Federer is taking a break in the snow. He posted a photo of himself holding a snowball and his tennis racket on Twitter. The 33-year-old wrote a funny caption, "tennice," and wore a scarf from his favorite football team, FC Basel. Federer skipped the Miami Open this year to protect his health.

Exeter beat Newcastle 48-13 to reach the first European Challenge Cup semi-final. They played Gloucester next. At Sandy Park, Exeter scored six tries while Newcastle scored one. David Ewers and a penalty try gave Exeter a 17-6 lead at half-time. After the break, Thomas Waldrom, Byron McGuigan, Sam Hill, and Dean Mumm all scored for Exeter. Newcastle only managed a try from Chris Harris and eight points from Tom Catterick in the second half. Carl Rimmer of Exeter was tackled by Newcastle's Dom Barrow.

On Thursday morning, 18-year-old Lewis Ferguson was doing his usual chores at Paul Nicholls' yard. He had a small cut on his nose from falling off a horse named Merrion Square at Wincanton on Wednesday. Videos of his scary double somersault fall have been watched online hundreds of thousands of times.

Ferguson said he was not discouraged from riding. He described the fall as a "blur" and said he did not understand what had happened until he saw the replay in the weighing room.

An Australian goanna was filmed eating a whole rabbit in less than one minute. The two-metre long lizard balanced on top of a power pole while swallowing its meal. It swung its neck back and forth to push the prey down its throat. The video starts at the top of a tall power pole, where the goanna is holding the rabbit. In Aboriginal mythology, goannas can unhinge their lower jaws to eat large prey.

Saracens chairman Nigel Wray called rugby’s salary cap rules a 'farce' in financial documents. These documents show the club's wage bill increased by £1million last season. This comes as Saracens face an investigation for breaking the salary cap rules. A few months ago, it was revealed the club is being investigated. The Mail on Sunday reports that Saracens' debt has now reached £40million, which is a record amount in rugby history.

Liam Plunkett, 29, is ready to bowl fast against the West Indies batsmen. He is back in the England Test team after missing last summer due to injury. Before his injury, he took 18 wickets in four Tests. Plunkett wants to use his speed to help England win the series. He returned to the England team last summer for matches against Sri Lanka and India. He recovered from a minor ankle injury during Yorkshire's trip to Abu Dhabi.

Martin Guptill has been selected for New Zealand's Test team to play England next month. This will be his first Test appearance since 2013. He is known for scoring 237 runs against the West Indies in a recent World Cup match.

Matt Henry, a fast bowler, has also been selected for the Test squad for the first time. He previously played in World Cup semi-finals and the final. He has only played 20 first-class matches.

England have only just arrived in St Kitts, but they are already ready to give Jonathan Trott a chance to open the batting. Trott, who usually bats at number three, spent four years as England's rock at that position before he had to leave the 2013-14 Ashes tour in Australia due to a stress-related illness.

He fought his way back into the team for this three-Test tour of the Caribbean. Although there was a lot of talk about Kevin Pietersen before the team left, the main focus of the tour is likely to be on Trott, the South African-born batsman. He was seen practicing in the nets, and he could be ready to play.

England Test captain Alastair Cook thought Jonathan Trott's career was finished 18 months ago. However, Cook now feels Trott is ready to handle the pressure again. Trott left the 2013/14 Ashes tour after just one match at the Gabba because he was struggling with anxiety. Cook worried this would end Trott's time with England, but has seen him rebuild his career with focus and determination while playing for Warwickshire and during a tour with England Lions.

Barney Gibson became the youngest first-class cricketer in county history four years ago. He made his debut at just 15 years old in 2011. However, he only played one senior match and never played in the top team again. The 19-year-old has now decided to retire from the sport. He said it was a hard choice to stop playing so young. In his final game for the second team, he did not bat or keep wicket; instead, he bowled three overs.

The World Endurance Championship is stopping the use of grid girls. The series, which is famous for the Le Mans 24-hour race, made this change to be more progressive. Starting at the Silverstone race next week, there will be no grid girls. This decision has pleased many people but will upset those who are used to seeing models in revealing clothes standing by the cars before the race starts.

Dr Steve Peters, a sports psychiatrist, says he only gave Jonathan Trott the tools to fix his career. Trott returned to the England team on Thursday night. Everton manager Roberto Martinez says he is not worried about Romelu Lukaku. Lukaku has started working with high-powered agent Mino Raiola. Raiola is a very influential agent. Other famous players he represents include Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Paul Pogba, and Mario Balotelli.

A man died by suicide at Universal Studios in Hollywood, California, on Friday afternoon. He shot himself in a smoking area near the Despicable Me ride around 2:15pm. Witnesses reported that crowds ran away in chaos after the incident. The man's identity has not been released.

Real Madrid really wants to sign Manchester United's goalkeeper, David De Gea. However, they are willing to wait until next summer if United's manager, Louis van Gaal, refuses to talk. De Gea has played very well this season. Meanwhile, Real Madrid's current goalkeeper, Iker Casillas, is considered unreliable. Even though Real wants to sign De Gea in June, they are also considering Chelsea's Petr Cech as an option. De Gea's current contract at United expires next year. In the Spanish newspapers, AS focuses on the attempt to sign De Gea, while Marca focuses on James Rodriguez.

John Carver has learned that a Tyne-Wear derby can decide if a manager keeps their job. He first worked in the dugout in 1999 as an assistant to Ruud Gullit. On a rainy night at St James' Park, Gullit left out Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson. The team lost 2-1, and Gullit was sacked.

Carver is currently trying to keep his job as head coach. He knows that the result of the upcoming derby against Sunderland on Sunday could decide his future. He is excited to manage his hometown team. In 1999, Gullit made a controversial decision to leave Shearer and Ferguson out of the starting lineup.

Louis van Gaal says Manchester United can still win the Barclays Premier League. His team is currently eight points behind the leaders, Chelsea, having played one extra game. Van Gaal also said that Marouane Fellaini has become almost impossible to leave out of the team because of his good form. If United wins against Aston Villa on Saturday, it will put pressure on Manchester City, who are currently second but do not play until Monday.

Frank Lampard said he would love to see a gay footballer come out and be respected. He appeared on a TV show called "Alan Carr's Chatty Man" with other celebrities. He believes football is changing and becoming less "macho." When the host asked if a gay player would ever appear, Lampard agreed, saying that with so many professional players, one must be gay.

Ryan Bertrand posted a photo on Instagram of himself and his daughter in matching red cars. The 25-year-old Southampton player gave his daughter a red Ferrari, similar to his own. He posed with her outside their home. Bertrand has played 26 Premier League games for Southampton this season after moving from Chelsea.

Dick Advocaat will not make the same mistake he made in 1998. The 67-year-old takes charge of Sunderland for the first time at home tomorrow against Newcastle. Back then, he said the Old Firm derby was "just another game," and Celtic won 5-1. He was heavily criticized for underestimating the rivalry. Now, Advocaat insists he understands the importance of the Wear-Tyne Derby and is preparing his team for the crucial match on Sunday.

Danny Cipriani helped Sale Sharks win 23-6 against Gloucester last Saturday. He scored 13 points with his kicking. Because Sale is out of the European competition, Cipriani has the weekend off. He flew to Dubai for a short break to rest before the final four games of the Aviva Premiership.

Lexi Thompson, now 20, is a professional golfer. She first played in the U.S. Women's Open when she was just 12 years old, making her the youngest person ever to compete in that tournament. Thompson has won six professional championships and has earned almost $3 million in her career. She will pose on the cover of the May edition of Golf Digest, using a towel to cover her chest.

A home owned by President Richard Nixon, known as the "Western White House," is now for sale for $75 million. The house sits on a 5.45-acre estate in San Clemente, California. Nixon bought the property in 1969, six months after he became president. The home, called "La Casa Pacifica," was built in 1926 and looks out over the Pacific Ocean. Nixon entertained 17 world leaders there, including Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev.

A fan waited for almost an hour to see Ryan Taylor for just five seconds before Sunday's Tyne-Wear derby. There was a quick photo and a good-luck message. He is one of the few players truly respected by Newcastle's disappointed fans. Taylor scored the winning goal at the Stadium of Light three years ago. This earned him a chant from the crowd and a place in the club's history. However, the fans like him for more than just that one goal against their rivals.

Brazilian football player Ratinho has a new, very unusual hairstyle. During a Brazilian Cup game on Thursday, the 35-year-old had hexagon shapes shaved into his head to look like a football. His team, Remo, played against Atletico PR and the game ended in a 1-1 draw after Igor Joao scored in the 76th minute.

Arsenal are happy and ready to play Liverpool on Saturday at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal is third in the league, six points ahead of Liverpool. In training on Friday, the players looked relaxed. They slapped defender Laurent Koscielny as a joke. Manager Arsene Wenger is happy after his team won all six matches in March and he won the Manager of the Month award.

Neymar and his Barcelona teammate Dani Alves went to watch Barcelona's basketball team play Real Madrid in a game called "El Clasico" on Thursday. Barcelona won the game 85-80. Neymar took a selfie with Dani Alves and his sister Rafaella while watching the match. Even though Barcelona won, Real Madrid is still in first place in their division by just a small number of points. Over the weekend, Neymar played for Brazil and beat Chile 1-0, but he had to deal with some very rough challenges from the Chilean players.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger does not know exactly why Alexis Sanchez chose the Emirates Stadium instead of Anfield. However, he is happy the Chile forward will play for his team instead of against them on Saturday. Sanchez had many choices after Barcelona let him leave. After the World Cup, the 26-year-old decided to continue his career under Wenger's guidance. He made a strong start in English football. The French coach also admits that Liverpool might have used their interest in Sanchez to help negotiate the move of Luis Suarez to Barcelona last summer.

In the next few weeks, Louis van Gaal will have lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson. On Friday, Van Gaal joked that Ferguson should pay for the meal. More importantly, Van Gaal wants to discuss real progress with Ferguson. Ferguson has waited a long time to hear good news. The team he left for David Moyes got worse, but the current Manchester United team has only looked purposeful sometimes under Van Gaal.

Northampton's controversial player, Courtney Lawes, is ready to play aggressively in France. He arrived with the Saints team for a big Champions Cup game against Clermont Auvergne. Lawes is known for a dangerous tackle on France player Jules Plisson during a match at Twickenham in the Six Nations. Although match officials decided no punishment was needed, many people, including in France and England, still criticize him for being too rough.

Juan Mata says Wayne Rooney tells him every day that England can win Euro 2016 in France. Mata, who plays for Manchester United, noted that Rooney scored his 47th England goal in a 4-0 win against Lithuania last week.

Anthony Joshua thinks his hunger and determination will be enough to beat Jason Gavern on Saturday. This will be Joshua's first fight of 2015, after he pulled out of a January match because of a back injury. The London 2012 gold medallist is unbeaten in 10 pro fights but has never gone past the third round. Gavern, however, is a veteran, stepping into the ring for the 50th time in his career.

Raheem Sterling and Theo Walcott will likely play against each other at the Emirates on Saturday. They are at very different points in their careers. Theo Walcott, who is 26, might be a warning to Sterling, who is 20, that early talent does not always lead to a successful career. Both players are currently negotiating new contracts with their clubs. Brendan Rodgers has praised Walcott in the past, and Arsene Wenger is a big fan of Sterling. It is possible that the two clubs could swap the players.

Sir Alex Ferguson is a famous manager who helped players like Ryan Giggs, David Beckham, and Cristiano Ronaldo become stars. He thinks Barcelona's Neymar is very talented, but says the 23-year-old is not quite as good as the best players in the world yet. He believes Neymar can eventually reach the level of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, but he still has some way to go.

Spain manager Vicente del Bosque was very surprised that his strong team could not score, even though they were dominating the game. Despite having control, Holland scored two goals through Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen to win 2-0. Del Bosque was most frustrated that Spain missed easy chances in front of the goal. Holland's Stefan de Vrij scored first by meeting a cross from Wesley Sneijder. Just four minutes later, Davy Klaassen scored after David de Gea saved his own shot.

An 18-year-old inmate at the Lower Buckeye Jail in Phoenix attacked two officers. The attack happened after the young man, who had been at the jail for two weeks, was seen walking in a room he was not allowed to be in. The officers told him to go back to his cell, but he began hitting them. One officer was hospitalized with a brain bleed and broken facial bones.

Former Marseille boss Jose Anigo says Zlatan Ibrahimovic would have been a hero at the Stade Velodrome if he had followed the path of Eric Cantona. This comes after Peter Schmeichel compared the 33-year-old to Cantona, suggesting he has the personality to become a great at Manchester United like the Frenchman.

It is said that eating slowly helps you enjoy the taste and texture of food. However, a video shows that Cooper the Labrador does not care about being a "food expert." Katie Gallegos from Clackamas County, Oregon, took Cooper and her friend Daisy to a McDonald's drive-thru for ice cream. While the small female dog took a few ladylike licks, Cooper ate the rest of the cone in one bite. Gallegos, who runs Dogpatch Resort, says Cooper always eats very quickly, so she always makes sure Daisy gets to eat first. The video of Cooper's ice cream outing has been watched more than seven million times.

Cape Verde is a group of islands about 400 miles off the coast of Senegal in Africa. The country has about 500,000 people and is known for its beautiful beaches and volcanic landscapes.

Cape Verde recently beat Portugal 2-0 in a major international football match. This was a surprising result because Portugal is a much bigger and more famous team. Before this match, many people wondered if Cape Verde had any football tradition. The answer is yes; the country has a strong passion for the sport, and this victory proves they are becoming a serious force in international football.

A spring-breaker was terrified when a manatee swam past her in Florida. She was heard screaming and begging for help while treading water. The video was taken with a selfie stick. The manatee is a harmless, plant-eating animal.

A man in China named Xu was arrested for buying a wife for his son. He is accused of human trafficking. Xu wanted to become a grandfather, so he bought a woman for his son. His son has learning difficulties. Xu tried to get the woman pregnant himself because his son had not slept with her. He realized the woman was infertile, so he sold her to another family. Xu is from Lianyungang city in eastern China.

Despite the rumors about his future at Manchester United, Radamel Falcao seems calm. Falcao has struggled to get a regular spot in the team and has even cried because he hasn't been playing much. However, he looks happier now. On Thursday, he went out to eat in Alderley Edge with a friend and then got into his £100,000 Porsche Panamera, which was waiting for him at a Waitrose car park. Falcao will decide his Manchester United future at the end of this season.

Cardiff City will not have any fans at their Championship game against Leeds United on Saturday. The Welsh club gave back their 500 tickets to support fans who are boycotting the trip. This is because both clubs have a history of fan trouble. Leeds United has not said why they are only giving a small number of tickets to away fans, when they usually give over 2,500.

Sportsmail's Derek Lawrenson is making his predictions for the 79th Masters at Augusta on Thursday. He thinks the best American player is Dustin Johnson. There are many great American players, but since Augusta often favors a story of redemption—like Vijay Singh or Adam Scott—Lawrenson chose Johnson. He believes Johnson needs to use his brain to match his huge driving distance. Dustin Johnson hit balls on the Augusta course on Wednesday. For the best European player (who is not from the UK), there are not many good options.

A 66-year-old man named Stephen John Docherty pleaded guilty to hurting someone on purpose. He did this because he was angry about concrete work at his house.

According to police, Mr. Docherty had hired a man to do the concrete work. On March 17, around 3:30 pm, Mr. Docherty got very angry when he saw the work was not finished how he wanted it. He then hurt the other man with a metal hook.

A cat named Simba was stuck under a bathtub for 27 days in Meckenheim, Germany. His owners, Helga and Eberhard Henkel, had looked for him since early March. A neighbor heard scratching sounds from under the tub and called the fire department. Firefighters rescued Simba, and he was reunited with his owners.

Santiago Vergini, a 26-year-old from Argentina, is thinking about staying at Sunderland. He returned on loan in August and has played 35 games this season. He started in the 1-0 win over Newcastle on Sunday, which helped the team's chances of staying in the Premier League. He wants to stay at the club permanently if they survive the drop.

Former Valencia striker Aritz Aduriz scored in the 90th minute to make the score 1-1 against his old team. Valencia had been playing with one less player after Nicolas Otamendi was sent off eight minutes earlier for a dangerous challenge. Substitute Rodrigo De Paul had given Valencia the lead before Aduriz equalized at the death.

A raccoon got stuck on a flag pole outside a church in Philadelphia on Tuesday. The animal was about 30 feet up. Video shows the raccoon clinging to the pole. It is not clear how the animal got up there.

A 21-year-old rapper named Keaway Lafonz Ivy was shot and killed while making a music video in Maryland on Wednesday. Police say a gun being used as a prop in the video went off, and one of the people with Ivy fired it. Ivy was hit in the chest and died at the scene near 62nd Place and Eastern Avenue in Seat Pleasant. On Friday, police arrested 21-year-old Lafonzo Leonard Iracks and charged him in connection with the killing.

MI5 has warned that workers in Britain's nuclear, transport, and public services could be a security risk after a pilot named Andreas Lubitz crashed a plane into the Alps, killing 150 people. Because of this, security sources say that even with physical security, it is very hard to stop someone already inside from causing harm. MI5 is now giving advice to protect "insiders," or employees working in sensitive areas, following the Germanwings disaster.

A man went to the hospital after he swallowed a whole beer bottle at a family gathering in Wagaman, Darwin, on Wednesday night. The 38-year-old man had chewed and swallowed the glass bottle and then lay down. His family called the hospital, and paramedics were called to the home. Superintendent Louise Jorgensen said police are frustrated by reports of drunk and foolish behavior.

About 1,500 migrants were saved by the Italian navy and coast guard in less than a day. On Saturday, coast guard ships helped five boats in the southern Mediterranean. New figures show that 43% more migrants have arrived in Italy this year compared to last year.
